evidence: The reviewer itself says 'this is not a bug today' and offers documenting the trust boundary as an option; every caller escapes its own values. The agent documented the contract in 023cb17 and declined a one-seam SafeHtml brand because escapeHtml and every fragment builder return string, so the brand would be cast-laundered. That reasoning holds for this layer.
guidance_note: When a function injects some parameters raw and escapes others, state the trust contract at the signature in the original PR instead of a one-line note.

evidence: This duplicates F1 for the body parameter alone and concedes 'no bug exists today'. The same 023cb17 doc-comment fix and the same reasoning against a lone brand apply.

Flag false positive: 023cb17 only rewrote the renderPageShell comment. The '(prefers-color-scheme:dark)' versus '(prefers-color-scheme: dark)' mismatch was in the original THEME_RESOLVER and THEME_TOGGLE_SCRIPT. The inconsistency is real but has no functional effect, and b4d468c aligned the strings.
guidance_note: When a module carries a copied twin of another file's script, copy every literal byte-identically, including the strings in newly written siblings.

evidence: setItem can throw, but an uncaught throw in a listener is logged to the console, so the claim that 'no error [is] surfaced' is false. The suggested try/catch with no reporting channel would be the actual silent swallow. The flagged code is original, not from 023cb17, and it mirrors index.html's shipped toggle.

This is the same shape as F4. An unavailable localStorage would already throw in THEME_RESOLVER's getItem in <head>, and an uncaught listener error is visible in the console, so 'no error is visible' is wrong. Wrapping it in try/catch would hide it. The code is original.

Flag false positive: 023cb17 never touched playgroundPages.test.ts. The direct playgroundCard tests covered only prompt escaping and the link, even though the card is exported for reuse. b4d468c added byline, provider, step-count, fork, and hostile-author tests.
guidance_note: When exporting a unit specifically for reuse by another surface, test its full rendered contract directly in the same PR, not only through the current composite caller.

evidence: Flag false positive: b4d468c touched only the matchMedia string and tests. This re-raises F1/F2's declined brand against the 023cb17 comment, and the finding itself says 'this is an informed design choice, not an oversight'. No defect was introduced.

The reviewer concedes 'all three correctly apply escapeHtml once each'. The 'fragility' is a hypothetical misuse that the documented contract (title arrives raw) already forbids. renderPlayer's title predates b4d468c, which only changed tests and one matchMedia string.

narrative: All four round-1 findings and both round-2 findings carry the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag, but each targets code that predates the named commit: 023cb17 was comment-only, and b4d468c was one string plus tests. The agent correctly declined two try/catch suggestions that would have created the silent swallow the reviewer cited no-silent-failure against. It also documented the trust contract rather than bolting on a cast-laundered brand. No fix in this PR caused a later finding.
guidance_observations: The reviewer re-raised the declined SafeHtml brand in round 2 even though it called the choice deliberate; the agent's 'already addressed' resolution cost nothing.
The flagged localStorage and matchMedia items were judged on what an uncaught listener error actually does (it logs), not on the reviewer's 'silent' label.

evidence: The client's `by ${summary.author} · ${steps} step${...}` duplicates the server's byline/stepLabel. The agent rightly refused to put pre-formatted presentation strings into the PlaygroundSummary data projection and documented the coupling in 73a5096. Its claim that the duplication was 'irreducible' was overstated: PR #32 later removed it with a build-time generator. Deferring was still a defensible scope call.
guidance_note: Before calling a cross-surface duplication irreducible, check whether a build-time generation step could derive both copies from one source, and file that ticket instead of only commenting.

narrative: One advisory duplication finding. The agent rejected the reviewer's data-seam fix on sound grounds and documented the coupling. The second round was a clean approval.
guidance_observations: The 'irreducible' framing was disproved two PRs later (#32 generated the twin at build time), so the honest wording was 'deferred to a build step'.

evidence: The fixture carries XSS in both prompt and recipe, so the whole-page toContain('<script>') could pass from the h1 or recipe block. 1191226 extracts the meta content attribute and asserts there.
guidance_note: When a test name claims a location ('in an escaped meta description'), assert on that extracted location, especially when the fixture plants the same hostile value elsewhere on the page.

evidence: Flag false positive: 1191226 changed only playgroundPages.test.ts, and the quoted description template was original. The reviewer says 'Not a bug', and nested quotes are a minor cosmetic issue, so accepting a cheap rewording (fb1fc82) was fine. types-are-the-program has nothing to do with prose quote marks.

narrative: Round 0 caught a real test-location gap, fixed precisely. Round 1 raised a cosmetic point about the original description text, which the agent accepted while echoing the reviewer's inapt law tag. Round 2 was clean.
guidance_observations: The agent repeated the reviewer's law token on a cosmetic change instead of citing none; law tags on preference edits dilute the citation system.

evidence: `tp:[a-z]+` cannot match `tp:FOO`, so a mixed-case leftover marker would ship silently, which contradicts 'No marker may survive'. c6309bb widened it to [a-zA-Z]+ and tested `tp:Bogus`. A marker beginning with a digit would still evade the guard.
guidance_note: Write a leftover-marker guard to match anything after the marker prefix up to the comment terminator, not a guessed character class of today's names.

evidence: The comment named a nonexistent frontDoorChrome.test.ts. Instead of repointing it, c6309bb moved the lockstep assertion into a new frontDoorChrome.test.ts. That is the right boundary, since the test needs only that module's exports.
guidance_note: Before committing a module header that names files and mechanisms, check every named file and mechanism exists as described.

evidence: c6309bb did not touch frontDoorChrome.ts's header, which still claimed inlining 'via .toString()' even though the code splices the CARD_FORMAT_JS literal. F2 had already exposed drift in this same file's comments, and its fix did not sweep the rest of the header. e0f60e6 rewrote it.
guidance_note: When a reviewer finds one stale claim in a file's comments, reread every claim in that comment block against the code before pushing the fix.

evidence: Flag false positive: e0f60e6 was comment-only, and the one-shot `gen-index && tsx watch` dev script was original. The stale-homepage drift during dev is real. 1d3abff derived the page in-process in main.dev.ts so each watch restart regenerates it.
guidance_note: When introducing a build-time generated artifact, design the dev loop so the artifact regenerates on the same trigger that reloads its sources.

evidence: The F1 fix in c6309bb rewrote the leftover-marker test for casing only (`<!--tp:Bogus-->`). The guard's `/*` alternation branch stayed unexercised. 1d3abff added a `/*tp:Extra*/` case.
guidance_note: When fixing a guard regex, write one test per alternation branch and per character-class edge, not only for the axis the finding named.

narrative: This PR consolidated the chrome twins behind a build-time generator. Two fixes were narrow: F2's comment-drift fix left another stale claim in the same header (F3), and F1's guard fix tested only the casing axis, leaving the CSS-comment branch untested (F5). The round-1 summary also reported the committed index.html was not regenerated, which was not raised inline. Round 3 was clean.
guidance_observations: Both chains are 'fixed the instance named, didn't sweep the sibling': a header comment block and a regex's alternation branches.
A generated artifact committed alongside its generator needs the build run before every push; the round-1 summary caught a stale index.html.

evidence: toContain('tools') cannot prove no spurious tag fired, which is the negative the test's name claims. 7ca57a9 tightened it to toEqual(['tools']).
guidance_note: A test named for a negative property ('not accidental substrings') must assert the exact result set, not membership.

evidence: toBeLessThanOrEqual(5) passes for any five matches, even though the comment promises priority order. 7ca57a9 asserts exactly ['math','physics','game','audio','graphics'].
guidance_note: When the code comment promises an ordering property, the test must pin the exact ordered output.

evidence: The reviewer's trace is right: /[^a-z0-9]+/g → '-' then trimming turns ' C.S.S ' into 'c-s-s', not 'css'. 7ca57a9 corrected the comment examples.
guidance_note: Run each worked example in a normalizer's comment through the function before committing it.

evidence: Flag false positive: 7ca57a9 touched only tests and the types.ts comment, and the unescaped keywords.join('|') in deriveTags.ts was original. No current keyword contains a metacharacter, so the risk is latent. 96d3594 added a load-time ^[a-z0-9]+$ assertion, one of the reviewer's offered options.
guidance_note: When interpolating data into a RegExp, enforce the data's alphabet at load time in the same commit.

evidence: \btext does fire on 'texture'. However, right-anchoring would break deliberate stems ('simulat', 'visualiz', 'geometr') and plurals, which the vocabulary depends on. Documenting recall-over-precision behind the replaceable deriveTags seam is a sound trade. The code was original, not from 7ca57a9.
guidance_note: State a classifier's known precision trade-off next to the matcher in the original PR so a reviewer reads it as a decision.

evidence: The fork path also creates through persist→deriveTags, but only submit's tags were asserted. 96d3594 added `child.session.tags` contains 'tools'. Flag false positive: 7ca57a9 did not touch generationService.test.ts.
guidance_note: When a new step runs on every create path, assert it on each create entry point (submit and fork), not only the first.

narrative: Round 0 found two weak test assertions and a comment whose example did not match the normalizer; all were fixed precisely. Round 1's three findings target original deriveTags and generation test code, not the test/comment-only 7ca57a9. The agent reasonably kept prefix matching and documented it. Round 2 was clean.
guidance_observations: Every round-0 finding was a claim in a test name or comment that the assertion or code did not back; checking those claims before pushing would have removed the round.

evidence: The only tagFacets case had distinct counts, so the lexicographic tie-break never ran. dd9b71e's single summary tagged [b, a] makes a missing or inverted tie-break return [b, a] and fail.
guidance_note: For every comparator with a secondary key, add one input where the primary key ties.

evidence: The `commons` helper derives facets from results, so it cannot produce production's empty-results/non-empty-facets view. dd9b71e calls renderCommons directly with results:[] and a css facet.
guidance_note: When a test helper couples inputs that production keeps independent, add a direct test with the production combination.

evidence: Flag false positive: dd9b71e was tests only, and the inline renderCommons({...}) in siteHandler was original. The reviewer overstated it, since `all` and `query` were already named locals, as the agent noted. Lifting results/facets into locals is a small readability gain, not a decomposition issue.

Flag false positive: c70c5c2 only touched siteHandler.ts. COMMONS_STYLES' hardcoded rgba(99,102,241,0.12) was original and contradicted its own 'reads only shared design tokens' comment. 36b2096 introduced --focus-ring and used it at all three sites.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that claims CSS 'reads only shared tokens', grep the block for literal colors.

evidence: 36b2096 added --focus-ring only under :root. Neighbouring accent-derived tokens (--shadow-widget, --step-icon-bg) have [data-theme=dark] overrides, so the new token broke the system's pattern. dfe3e98 added the dark override.
guidance_note: When lifting a literal into a design token, check every theme block the sibling tokens are defined in and define the new token in each.

evidence: renderCommons(array) is a TypeScript compile error against the exported CommonsView, and all in-repo callers were updated. In a single-repo pre-release app, a 'future consumer on the old signature' cannot reach runtime. The signature change is original PR code, not from 36b2096.
This is the same missing dark override as F5, seen in the generated index.html from 36b2096. It was fixed at the frontDoorChrome source and regenerated in dfe3e98.
guidance_note: When lifting a literal into a design token, define it in every theme block its siblings appear in.

evidence: Flag false positive: dfe3e98 only added a CSS token. normalizeTag's ASCII-only [^a-z0-9] and its exposure through tryTag to URL params were original. Because of that ASCII-only class, ?tag=café silently became 'caf'. 70d1da9 switched to [^\p{L}\p{N}]+ with the u flag. That commit merged about 30 seconds after the reply, with no review round on it.
guidance_note: When a normalizer is newly exposed to user input (tryTag on URL params), enumerate non-ASCII and other out-of-vocabulary inputs in that PR's tests.

narrative: Most flagged findings target original PR code rather than the named fix commits, which were small, test-only, or local renames. The one real chain is F4's --focus-ring token added only to the light theme, which produced F5 and F7 and the extra round 4. The final Unicode normalizer change (70d1da9) merged right after being pushed, with no review round on it.
guidance_observations: The reviewer surfaced new findings in original code each round (F4, F6, F8), stretching the PR to five rounds; only round 4 traces to an incomplete fix.
A behavior change to tag normalization merged without any review pass on the commit that made it.

evidence: Option B said 'the card shows the Option-A placeholder until the real thumbnail exists', while the Decision says 'no gradient-placeholder interim'. The agent admits the Decision rewrite left the stale text. 448291a fixed both Option A and Option B.
guidance_note: When a decision supersedes an option, search the whole doc for every sentence that prescribes the superseded behavior before committing.

evidence: 'Verified end-to-end' (in dev) and 'generation disabled at first public deploy' are not strictly contradictory, but a reader could take them that way. 448291a added a one-sentence reconciliation.
An empty-until-rendered slot hides no error, so citing no-silent-failure for the UX choice was a misfit. 448291a replaced it with [FRAMING:representation] and plain-language reasoning.
guidance_note: Cite a law token only where the sentence names the failure that law prohibits; otherwise state the reasoning in prose.

evidence: Cache-versus-source drift is a one-source-of-truth concern, and the doc already cites that law a few lines earlier. 448291a retagged it.
guidance_note: Cite a law token only where the sentence names the failure that law prohibits.

evidence: Flag false positive: 448291a did not touch Option C's `playgroundPages.ts:472` citation. :472 is the rationale comment, which is defensible for 'deliberately', but the attribute is at :504. 733505a cites both.

The [FRAMING:representation] token was introduced by the F3 fix in 448291a. The agent's rebuttal holds: FRAMING tokens are a deliberate second namespace for reasoning documents, and the sentence states its meaning in plain language before the tag. No change was needed.

Flag false positive: 733505a only changed a line reference, and the 'Every account gets a free allotment' text was original. The reviewer missed that GitHub OAuth accounts already exist. The agent corrected that premise and recorded that credits resolve the creation half, rather than marking the decision provisional.
guidance_note: When recording a decision whose premise depends on another open decision, state in the same entry which part of the open one it settles.

evidence: The proposal drops the homelab staging rehearsal while 2YEARPLAN.mnd line 95 still described it. The text is original. ea527c4 updated 2YEARPLAN at the source.
guidance_note: When a proposal changes the roadmap, update every roadmap doc that states the old plan in the same PR.

evidence: BlobStore.write takes Artifact = { html: string }, so 'under the existing BlobStore seam' cannot hold a PNG. The text is original. ea527c4 states that the seam must be extended to carry bytes.
guidance_note: When a design doc claims an existing seam fits a new payload, check the seam's signature before citing it.

evidence: 'Same key space as the .html' with BlobStore keyed by VersionId alone means a thumbnail write would clobber the artifact. The text is original. ea527c4 specified a distinct thumb/<versionId> key.
guidance_note: When a design doc places a second blob next to an existing one, say how the two keys differ.

evidence: An async render with no retry or failure surfacing leaves 'not yet' indistinguishable from 'failed forever'. The text is original. ea527c4 added a bounded retry and a failed-to-render flag.
guidance_note: Every async job in a design doc gets its failure path specified: retry bound, terminal state, and where that state lives.

evidence: ea527c4 (the F7 fix) wrote that credits 'resolve the creation half of the still-open accounts vs. anonymous decision'. It left the Open decisions bullet reading as fully open. 93ef028 narrowed that bullet.
guidance_note: When a fix says it settles part of another listed item, edit that item in the same commit.

evidence: Flag false positive: the 'enqueue render version X on publish' trigger with no named seam was original text. ea527c4 only appended retry wording to that bullet. 93ef028 named the post-publish web-layer hook and excluded finalizeSuccess.
guidance_note: When a design forbids putting a trigger in one place, name the place it goes.

evidence: 'disabled/tunneled' is ambiguous between off and proxied. Flag false positive: the phrase was in the original PROJECT.md text, not from 93ef028, though ea527c4 copied it into 2YEARPLAN. eab618c rephrased it in both places.

ea527c4 (the F11 fix) introduced a 'flagged failed-to-render' state but gave the flag no home, even though the doc rejects putting thumbnail data on the catalog record. eab618c named a VersionId-keyed status entry owned by the render pipeline.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a new state, say where that state is stored in the same edit, especially when the doc has already ruled out the obvious home.

narrative: This design-doc PR drew fifteen findings over five rounds. Most were real original-text gaps (seam typing, key collision, render failure path, cross-doc roadmap drift) that the agent accepted. Three fixes spawned follow-ups: a new FRAMING token (correctly defended), a decision note that left its sibling Open-decisions bullet stale, and a failed-to-render flag with no storage home. Each later round also had a non-caused finding, so no round was purely avoidable. The final fixes (eab618c) merged without a review pass.
guidance_observations: Design-doc fixes that add a new state or settle part of another item spawned the follow-ups; each fix should be read against the rest of the doc before pushing.
The reviewer found new original-text issues every round (F7-F11, F13, F14), which suggests the first-round review was shallow on a design doc.
